messages.subject: Some questions about renjin when I try it
parts:
When I try to use renjin these days, It really attract me. But there
are some questions about the renjin,can you give me some suggestions?
1. performance benchmarks
can you give me some suggestions about the benchmarks, which can
run original R and renjin.thanks!


2."Calling into Java from R is now fully implemented via the import()
method"
When I read the source code,"import" can only load the classes
which are loaded by Bootstrap ClassLoader or Extension Classloader,
can I use some 'require' like commander to load external jar .
I just used -Xbootclasspath/a:hadoop.jar for short.


3.when I try to use kmeans in renjin, I got a error "Error:
'duplicated' is not yet implemented"
And I see kmeans in the stats package which use .C and .Fortran.
then it's not pure in R.
does it mean I can't use it with no modifing my code.

4.Is there a compiler like "javac" by which I can complier the *.R to
*.class, and then run it on jvm by "java" like execute tools?( when I
read the source code , I really have found compiler package, But how
it work? Can I use it?)

Hi Jiessie,Thanks for trying out Renjin!Responses below.

On Nov 24, 3:35 am, jiessie <jiessie....@gmail.com> wrote:> When I try

to use renjin these days, It really attract me. But there> are some
questions about the renjin,can you give me some suggestions?> 1.
performance benchmarks>     can you give me some suggestions about the
benchmarks, which can> run original R and renjin.thanks!

I've just committed updates to the benchmarks module, it's written in
R so you can run it in Renjin and the original interpreter. I've taken
many of the benchmarks from http://r.research.att.com/benchmarks/
See the README file in this module. Contributions are welcome!

> > 2."Calling into Java from R is now fully implemented via the import()> method">     When I read the source code,"import" can only  load the classes> which are loaded by Bootstrap ClassLoader or Extension Classloader,> can I use some 'require' like commander to load external jar .>    I just used -Xbootclasspath/a:hadoop.jar for short.>

Does it work if you add the jar to the normal classpath? I.e. java -cp
renjin-core.jar;hadoop.jar ? If not we may need to fix something.
It would probably also be useful to add an R function to allow adding
to the classpath at runtime. I'lllook into this.

> 3.when I try to use kmeans in renjin, I got a error "Error:> 'duplicated' is not yet implemented">   And I see kmeans in the stats package which use .C and .Fortran.> then it's not pure in R.>   does it mean I can't use it with no modifing my code.>

duplicated is an R primitive, it needs to be implemented in renjin-
core. (see http://code.google.com/p/renjin/wiki/AnnotationBasedImpl)
it looks like the kmeans function is mostly implemented in the "base
library" with nativecode, so you could implement the missing functions
in the r.base.Base class. (When you see .Call() with outa package
argument, it means that the implementation is in the base library)
The kmeans algorithm is pretty straightforward, so it should not take
much work to implement, or youcould even delegate to the Apache
Commons math implementation.

> 4.Is there a compiler like "javac" by which I can complier the *.R to> *.class, and then run it on jvm by "java" like  execute tools?( when I> read the source code , I really have found compiler package, But how> it work? Can I use it?)

The compiler is work in progress, I hope to have it up and running in
the next month or so, but from whatI've seen so far, I don't think an
Ahead of Time (AOT) compiler will be a good option, because most
optimizations will not be possible at compile-time because R is so
dynamic.
At runtime, however, like when a function is actually called, we know
alot more about the types of the variables, so a JIT compiler will
allow much more effective optimization.
So if you want to package R code in a jar (i.e if you want to deploy a
hadoop mapper written in R), you will have to write a wrapper class in
Java that loads the scripts from the classpath and makes the calls.
For example:
class MyRMapper extends Mapper {
  MyRMapper() {  /* init context and load script */ }
  void map(K key, V value) {     /* pass to R */  }}
I think in the future we could write a renjin-maven-plugin that could
automatically generate these wrapper classes and handle all the
packaging of R/Java code into a jar.
Would love to welcome you as a contributor, just send your first
changes as a patch, and then I will add you to google code so you can
commit directly!
Best,
Alex

Ah ok I see now. If you're looking to use the Renjin in an interactive way, the easiest (at present)

This obviously isn't actually "easy" -- Tony Kennedy is working on an eclipse plugin for Renjin
that will better address this use case.

> So if you want to package R code in a jar (i.e if you want to deploy a

Good idea! In this way we can use R handle the small partition of big
data.
Maybe the Wrapper class can be generated in Renjin interpreter or

I am not  familiar with OO in R, is it possible use R to implement a
subclass extends the super Mapper class without the java OO?

Not yet. The ObjectConverter class needs to be extended so that it can 
create implementations of interfaces at runtime / new subclasses of abstract class from an R object, either 
  a) a simple list of functions, e.g. x = list( map = function(key, value, context) { } )
  b) an S4 object
  c) an environment with functions (see the proto library)

Interfaces are not hard (we can use java proxying) but generating new subclasses on the fly 
may take a bit more more work.
I think writing mapreduce code in R is not very easy for user now.

Yes I think we still need to find the best way to address this use case. Actually two uses cases maybe:
1) RenjinMapper + maven plugin for bundling R source as a deployable jar to hadoop
2) Hadoop R library that enables the developer to submit map/reduce jobs written in R interactively to a cluster

But in another way, there are some java packages such as Apache
Mahout , if we can access HDFS in R, and  if we can call java from R
smoothly, and we can submit mahout jobs in R, and load the result with
HDFS API to make further analysis. So for the first step, I think
integrating R with Hadoop by this simple interactive way may be
easier.

You should already be able to access HDFS via Renjin with the HDFS plugin for Commons Virtual File System (VFS) that Renjin uses.
If you add the plugin to your classpath

And a question again? In orignal R, we can use "R CMD INSTALL" and
>install.packages('aspects') ,
what about Renjin?  I found that the lib folder is packaged into
renjin-core.jar, any other way to install the external packages?

Both R2.x and Renjin work in the same way in this regard: the base package maintains 
a search path for libraries (type .libPaths() into the REPL) which you can update by calling .libPaths("/path/to/my/lib")

Renjin initializes this list to your classpath on startup, plus the library folder in renjin-core.jar, if you have a folder 
with external packages you want to use, you can add this folder to your classpath. 

In Renjin, you can also use VFS URIs, so you could add .libPaths("jar:file://home/alex/aspect-1.0.jar") at runtime as well.
